title: Endings on the web build open over the last fight's song: ending_* and credits are streamed, never prefetched, and play() keeps the old track while downloading
repro: Web build, first time reaching an ending: Epilogue._ready calls play('ending_penguin'/'ending_gangster') (1.2-1.9 MB, not in PREFETCH). Music.play only starts a stand-in when nothing is playing, so the boss/area song from the final fight carries on under the slideshow until the download lands (epilogue comment says the ending must NOT be whatever the last fight left playing). Then credits (1.9 MB, also streamed) is requested on finish: the ending has stopped so the 'house' stand-in plays until credits arrive.
fix: Prefetch ending_<arc> and credits as soon as the final chapter opens (or when Epilogue is built, via a Music.prefetch(list) helper that jumps the queue). In play(), add a 'cut' option (or treat ONCE tracks so) that starts the stand-in immediately instead of letting the previous song continue; Epilogue passes it. Optional: move the two ending tracks into EMBED in tools/music_stream.py if pack size allows (~3 MB).

title: Song cache user://mcache has no version: a re-imported/swapped song (ace_batch --swap, --reimport-all) is never re-downloaded by phones that cached the old one
repro: Music._stream_for loads user://mcache/<name>.ogg if it exists and never checks it against the deployed file. data/music_stream.json lists only names. After any ACE swap the deploy ships the new music/<name>.ogg but every phone that heard the old version keeps playing it forever (Tom plays on the phone, so he would never hear fixes to songs he already visited).
fix: tools/music_stream.py writes a short content hash per track: {"stream": [...], "ver": {name: sha1[:8]}}; Music caches as user://mcache/<name>.<ver>.ogg, deletes other versions of that name when saving, and fetches <name>.ogg?v=<ver> so the HTTP/SW cache can't serve the old file either. Extend tools/music_stream_test.gd: a cached file with a stale ver is ignored and replaced.

title: Unbounded music memory on phones: every downloaded song stays in Music._streamed for the session and user://mcache (up to ~121 MB) is never pruned
repro: 87 streamed songs total 120.9 MB. _streamed keeps each AudioStreamOggVorbis built by load_from_buffer forever (WASM heap), _stream_for also reads the whole cache file into a temp PackedByteArray, and the cache directory only grows. On the Godot web build user:// is IDBFS, which Emscripten mirrors into MEMFS in memory and syncs at startup, so a full cache is loaded into the tab's memory on every boot. Phone Safari/Chrome kill tabs well before that adds up with the game's ~64 MB texture budget.
fix: Keep _streamed as a small LRU (current, fading, last 2-3; drop others after a crossfade ends). Cap user://mcache (e.g. 40 MB, by last-used order kept in a small index json; never evict PREFETCH songs of the current arc first). Add a perf/stream test check that _streamed size stays bounded after playing 15 tracks.

title: Prefetch can stall for the whole session when a prefetched song becomes the wanted song and its download fails
repro: Prefetch 'night' (_prefetching='night'), night falls -> play('night') (fetch already running). The download fails: _failed sees track == _current so it skips the prefetch branch and leaves _prefetching='night'. Morning comes before the retry timer fires -> callback does nothing (track != _current). _prefetch_next now returns early forever (_prefetching != ''), so no more songs are prefetched until 'night' is wanted again and succeeds.
fix: In _failed always clear _prefetching when track == _prefetching (and schedule _prefetch_next), then do the wanted-song retry separately. Add a case to tools/music_stream_test.gd (fail a prefetched song while wanted, change track, check another prefetch starts).

title: Arc theme songs (largest files, 2.6-2.9 MB) are never prefetched before the title arc choice, but are prefetched first once a run starts, where they are useless
repro: Title screen: run is empty, so _prefetch_next only uses PREFETCH (night, rain, town...). Picking an arc plays arc_penguins/arc_gangsters, which on a first visit almost never arrives before the character page is done (title keeps playing). After the run starts, PREFETCH_PENGUIN/GANG put arc_<arc> FIRST, spending ~2.7 MB of mobile bandwidth on a song only the title uses, delaying combat_light/danger/raid (first fight then plays the area song).
fix: While GameState.run is empty, prefetch arc_penguins and arc_gangsters first (title has ~10+ s before a choice). Remove arc_* from PREFETCH_GANG/PREFETCH_PENGUIN so in-run prefetch starts with combat_light(_gang) and danger/raid.

title: Fixed 45 s total HTTPRequest timeout makes the biggest songs fail forever on slow mobile data
repro: rq.timeout = 45.0 is the whole-request limit in Godot 4. title-size songs (arc_gangsters 2.85 MB, arc_penguins 2.59 MB, credits 1.94 MB) need > 45 s below ~500 kbit/s (weak 4G/3G, rural Spokane edges). Each retry restarts from byte 0, so the song never lands and the stand-in loops for the whole visit.
fix: Scale the timeout to the file (e.g. timeout = 0 / none, and instead watch get_downloaded_bytes() for 20 s of no progress) or set timeout = max(45, size_kb / 30) using a size list from tools/music_stream.py (the same json as the version hash).

title: Boss, keeper, mine and next-area songs are never prefetched: the first boss fight (and first mine visit) on the web build plays the previous area song
repro: All 13 BOSS_TRACKS, MEGA_BOSS themes, keeper, marked, mine/mine_deep and every mega area song are streamed (0.5-1.6 MB each) and only PREFETCH/PREFETCH_<arc> (17 songs) are fetched ahead. Music.play keeps the current song while downloading, so a boss intro/fight on a phone plays the calm area tune for 5-30 s (often the whole first fight on mobile data); walking into the mine keeps the meadow song. Probe: nothing outside music.gd ever calls _fetch/prefetch (grep).
fix: Add Music.prefetch(tracks: Array, front := false) that queues names ahead of the PREFETCH list (only if streamed and not cached). In GameMap._ready (small hook) call it with boss_track() when the map holds a boss/guardian, plus area_track() of each neighbour from GoalLine.adj(scene_id) (mine -> mine, keeper). Extend tools/music_stream_test.gd: after prefetch(['boss']) with force_stream, play('boss') starts at once.

title: Jukebox says it dropped a new record, but on the web the old song keeps playing until the record downloads
repro: RecCenter._jukebox plays juke_needle and toasts 'The jukebox clunks and drops a record: X', then Music.play(X). Every jukebox record (rec_center, jukebox_oldie, bowling_alley, arcade_hall, neon, ...) is streamed, so on a first visit the previous record/house song carries on for several seconds to half a minute after the toast.
fix: When the player enters the rec, Music.prefetch the next JUKEBOX record (the one _jukebox would pick) so the tap is instant; if it still isn't ready, show 'The jukebox warms up...' and toast the record name when Music reports it started (now_playing() == t).

title: title_musicbox is packed into the web download (0.88 MB) but nothing plays it (AUDIO-PLAN F5: save screen and creator)
repro: tools/music_stream.py EMBED = {title, farm, house, title_musicbox}; export pack check (godot --export-pack Web) confirms audio/music/title_musicbox is in the pck. grep: no script references title_musicbox (only music_stream.py and music_map_test.gd). docs/AUDIO-PLAN.md F5 says it belongs on the save screen and character creator.
fix: Wire it in title.gd (save-slot page and the character creator play title_musicbox, Back returns to title) - it is packed, so it starts instantly. If it stays unused, drop it from EMBED and rerun tools/music_stream.py.

title: No guard that data/music_stream.json, the export excludes and audio/music agree; the relative-URL test line is a tautology
repro: Today they agree (87 streamed = 87 excluded, 4 packed; export-pack probe shows only title/title_musicbox/farm/house in the pck and data/music_stream.json included). But a song excluded in export_presets.cfg without being in music_stream.json would be silent on the site (not packed, never fetched), and a new song added without rerunning music_stream.py silently bloats the pck; no test catches either. music_stream_test's last check `_base_url() == '' or begins_with('http')` always passes headless, so the web JavaScriptBridge path is untested.
fix: music_map_test: parse export_presets.cfg exclude_filter and assert the audio/music excludes == music_stream.json stream list, and every audio/music/*.ogg is either streamed or in the EMBED set (read from music_stream.json if music_stream.py writes 'embed'). Replace the tautology with a check of the URL builder on a fake baseURI (split the string logic out of _base_url into a static helper taking the base).

title: The wanted song shares bandwidth with an in-flight background prefetch (up to 2.9 MB) instead of pre-empting it
repro: _prefetch_next only checks _fetching is empty before starting, but play() -> _fetch(wanted) starts a second HTTPRequest while a prefetch (e.g. arc_gangsters 2.85 MB, first in PREFETCH_GANG) is still downloading; on mobile data both crawl, so the song the player is actually hearing late arrives even later.
fix: In _fetch for a wanted track (track == _current), cancel_request() + free the running prefetch HTTPRequest (clear _prefetching without counting a try) and resume prefetching from _got of the wanted song.

title: Deploy can ship an empty or partial music/ folder without failing (no pipefail, no count check, no smoke fetch)
repro: Export step: `python3 -c ... | while read t; do cp ...; done` runs without pipefail, so a python/JSON error yields zero copies and exit 0; nothing compares the number of files in build/web/music with the stream list. Every streamed song would then 404 on the site and only the farm/house/title stand-ins would ever play (the game itself would not show any error).
fix: Add `set -eo pipefail`, then `test $(ls build/web/music/*.ogg | wc -l) -eq $(python3 -c 'import json;print(len(json.load(open("data/music_stream.json"))["stream"]))')`, and after deploy-pages a curl -fsI of ${page_url}music/town.ogg.

title: While a wanted song downloads, ANY current song carries on: the title theme plays over a loaded save, combat/boss music lingers after a fight
repro: Music.play only uses a stand-in when nothing is playing (`_now == '' or not _player.playing`). Web, first session: load a save in fall/winter/rain or at night -> area_track is farm_fall/winter/rain/night (streamed; only 'night' is first in PREFETCH) -> the title (or arc_*) theme keeps playing on the farm until the file lands. Same rule after combat: if the area song was still downloading when a fight began, DangerMusic's return to area_track() leaves combat_light/danger/boss looping after the foes are gone.
fix: Keep the current song only if it is a calm area/interior song; if _now is title/title_musicbox/arc_*, a combat/danger/raid track, a BOSS_TRACKS/MEGA_BOSS song or a ONCE track, crossfade to _standin(track) instead. Add both cases to tools/music_stream_test.gd (play title -> play('farm_fall') with force_stream => farm stand-in; play cached combat_light -> play(uncached area) => stand-in).

title: AUDIO-PLAN says 57 songs stream; it is 87 (120.9 MB), and the cache/prefetch behaviour is undocumented
repro: docs/AUDIO-PLAN.md line 29: '57 songs stream on demand'. data/music_stream.json lists 87 (120.9 MB on Pages; 6.6 MB packed). Nothing documents PREFETCH lists, retry delays, or that user://mcache is never refreshed.
fix: Update the count/sizes and add two lines on prefetch order, cache versioning and the size cap once those fixes land.

title: Asking for the song that is already playing as a stand-in restarts it with a crossfade
repro: Web: wanted 'inn' while it downloads -> stand-in 'house' plays (_now='house', _current='inn'). Walk out and into the farmhouse: play('house') passes the `track == _current` guard, finds the packed stream and _start() crossfades house into a fresh copy of house from 0:00 (same with 'farm' as the outdoor stand-in when you step onto the farm).
fix: At the top of play(): if track == _now and _player.playing, set _current = track and return (no restart).
